stories.headline: Assam Earthquake: 4.1 Magnitude Tremors Felt in Guwahati
stories.title: Assam Earthquake: 4.1 Magnitude Tremors Felt in Guwahati
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: An earthquake measuring 4.1 on the Richter scale struck Assam at 2:43 pm on 14th November with tremors reported in Guwahati and nearby areas.
No casualties have been reported so far, while further information about the epicentre and depth of the earthquake is awaited.
The earthquake struck Assam at approximately 2:43 pm on.
The reported magnitude was 4.1 on the Richter scale.
Tremors were felt in Guwahati and nearby areas following the earthquake.
The quake was recorded at a depth of 10 km, on latitude 25.749 N and longitude 91.273 E with its epicentre in Assam's Kamrup district.
The initial information places the reported location approximately 8 km from Assam.
However, the precise epicentre and the depth of the earthquake have not been established in the available information.
The earthquake brought seismic activity to the attention of people in the affected areas.
However, the available information does not specify the number of locations where tremors were felt or the duration of the shaking.
The National Centre for Seismology (NCS) is the government agency responsible for monitoring and reporting seismic.
The exact epicentre and depth are also awaited.

stories.headline: AP SEC Reviews Panchayat Election Preparedness
stories.title: AP SEC Reviews Panchayat Election Preparedness
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha has reviewed election preparedness and security arrangements for the forthcoming gram panchayat polls, as well as pending urban local body elections.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha has reviewed election preparedness and security arrangements for the forthcoming gram panchayat polls, as well as pending urban local body elections.
Punetha met officials at the Tirupati Collectorate.
Senior police officers from 12 districts attended, and discussions focused on maintaining peace and security during the elections.
Speaking to the media afterwards, the SEC said there had been contests and election-related issues in areas from Palnadu to Rayalaseema during recent polls.
He had held discussions with police superintendents from 12 districts and urged them to remain especially vigilant during the panchayat elections.
Candidates who require an escort to file their nominations can request one, Punetha said.
He added that special security would be provided to candidates if police receive information about a threat of attack.
The Panchayat Raj Department has also issued new guidelines on incentives for villages that elect their panchayats unanimously.
Villages with populations of up to 5,000 will receive ₹15 lakh, while those with populations between 5,000 and 10,000 will be given ₹25 lakh.
Punetha said unanimous elections could take place in 15 to 20 per cent of villages.

stories.headline: Cluster of Block Sports Meet Concludes Successfully in Anantnag, Over 150 Youth Participate
stories.title: Cluster of Block Sports Meet Concludes Successfully in Anantnag, Over 150 Youth Participate
stories.summary: Anantnag, Nov 14: Promoting sportsmanship, physical fitness and a drug-free lifestyle among young people, MY Bharat Anantnag successfully concluded a two-day Cluster of Block Sports Meet at Sports Stadium Bijbehara on November 14, organised as part of the 9th Week of the 100 Weeks Campaign under the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan. The two day sporting event, held on November 13 and 14, 2026, was organised under the inspiring theme “Swasth Yuva Viksit Bharat” by MY Bharat Anantnag, functioning under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India. The initiative aimed at encouraging young people to adopt healthy lifestyles, participate in sports and contribute towards building a healthier, stronger and drug-free society. The event witnessed enthusiastic participation from more than 150 young participants, including MY Bharat Volunteers, Youth Club members and students from various educational institutions across the district. The participants displayed remarkable enthusiasm, sporting talent and team spirit throughout the competitions. A total of six sporting events were organised during the two-day programme, providing participants with an opportunity to showcase their abilities across different sporting disciplines. On the first day, a badminton competition for girls was held, witnessing active participation and competitive performances. The second day featured five sporting events, including Volleyball for Boys, Tug of War for Girls, Shot Put for Boys, a 100-Metre Race for Boys and Skipping Rope for Girls. The competitions created an atmosphere of excitement and healthy competition, with participants displaying determination, discipline and enthusiasm. The programme was organised with the broader objective of strengthening the sports culture at the grassroots level and providing young people with constructive platforms to showcase their abilities. It also highlighted the role of sports in developing confidence, leadership qualities, teamwork and discipline among youth. Addressing the gathering, the importance of engaging young people in positive activities and encouraging them to stay away from substance abuse was highlighted. The initiative also reflected the larger vision of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan, which seeks to mobilise youth towards a healthier, more responsible and progressive society. The occasion was graced by international cricketer Mr. Parvez Rasool, who attended the programme as the Chief Guest. International footballer Mr. Mohammad Salah and Mr. Mohammad Shafi, Manager, Sports Council, attended as Guests of Honour. Their presence added significance to the sporting event, while their encouragement and interaction with the participating youth served as a source of motivation for aspiring sportspersons. The participation of prominent sports personalities also underlined the importance of sports in shaping the future of young people and inspiring them to pursue their goals with dedication. At the conclusion of the competitions, certificates and prizes were distributed among the winners and participants in recognition of their performances, enthusiasm and sporting spirit. The organisers appreciated the participation of the youth and acknowledged their efforts in making the two day event a success. The successful conclusion of the Cluster of Block Sports Meet reaffirmed MY Bharat Anantnag’s commitment to promoting youth engagement through sports, awareness programmes and community based initiatives. Such activities are expected to encourage greater participation in physical activities while providing young people with meaningful opportunities to contribute to society. Through initiatives like these, MY Bharat continues to work towards nurturing a generation of healthy, disciplined and empowered young citizens, in line with the vision of a Nasha Mukt and Viksit Bharat.

But in emerging markets, the obvious market to benefit from the reverse AI trade has been India, most particularly with the recent disappointing election result in Brazil, he said.Chris Wood on FII returnThis is why it is no surprise to Wood that foreign investors have turned net buyers of Indian equities in the past three weeks, after a massive selloff at the beginning of 2025. Most importantly, there is accumulating evidence that a long anticipated private-sector capex cycle is finally happening, with the best chart supporting this view of the rising trend in the imports of machinery goods. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s comments in France at the G7 foreign ministers meeting suggests he favours a policy of intensifying economic pressure on Iran via the blockade. This is why it is no surprise to Wood that foreign investors have turned net buyers of Indian equities in the past three weeks, after a massive selloff at the beginning of 2025.

The other point that the ace investor pointed out is India’s attractive valuations, relative to history, which remains comparatively modest while the cyclical recovery in the economy this year has been better than expected.
The Nifty index and the Nifty MidCap 100 index are now trading at 18x and 23x one-year forward earnings respectively.

Most importantly, there is accumulating evidence that a long anticipated private-sector capex cycle is finally happening, with the best chart supporting this view of the rising trend in the imports of machinery goods.
They have more than doubled from $29 billion in FY21 to $62 billion in FY26.

These inflows totaled Rs 350 billion in October this year and Rs 3.9 trillion in the first ten months of 2026, or an average of $4.1 billion per month.

In this respect, India remains the most dynamic capital market in the world after the US, though directional terms for the benchmark indices have been capped by rising equity insuance to absorb these inflows.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump said this week that “Iran militarily is effectively over" and that renewed US strikes are "highly unlikely”.
However, the hopes of any peace deal still remain elusive.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s comments in France at the G7 foreign ministers meeting suggests he favours a policy of intensifying economic pressure on Iran via the blockade.
As for Iran the question is whether it decides to turn pre-emptive.
In this background, Jefferies will maintain energy stocks in the portfolios since they are the only way to hedge renewed geopolitical tensions.
This is another way of advising investors who do not own energy stocks to take advantage of the recent sharp decline to buy them.
“For such reasons GREED & fear will maintain energy stocks in the various GREED & fear portfolios as the only practical hedge available,” Wood wrote in his report.

stories.headline: Four earthquakes strike Jammu and Kashmir in 12 hours
stories.title: Four earthquakes strike Jammu and Kashmir in 12 hours
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 14: Four earthquakes of varying magnitudes struck Jammu and Kashmir over a period of around 11 hours on Saturday, with three of the tremors recorded in Doda district and one in Kishtwar. According to the earthquake data, the first tremor, measuring 3.3 on the Richter scale, was recorded in Kishtwar district at 2:38 am, at a depth of 15 kilometres. Three more earthquakes were subsequently recorded in Doda district. reported Kashmir Weather. The second earthquake, measuring 2.7 magnitude, struck at 8:31 am at a depth of 10 kilometres. Seventeen minutes later, at 8:48 am, another tremor measuring 3.8 magnitude was recorded in the district at a depth of five kilometres. The fourth earthquake, measuring 2.9 magnitude, was recorded at 1:09 pm in Doda district, at a depth of 10 kilometres. The repeated seismic activity was concentrated in the Doda–Kishtwar belt, with the strongest tremor measuring 3.8 magnitude.

stories.headline: India Shines at Youth Olympics with Historic 10-Medal Haul, Including Two Golds
stories.title: India Shines at Youth Olympics with Historic 10-Medal Haul, Including Two Golds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: India signed off from the 2026 Summer Youth Olympic Games in Dakar with 10 medals, including two gold, three silver and five bronze, marking the country’s second-best performance in the history of the competition.
India’s medal-winning campaign spanned seven disciplines, with five Khelo India Athletes among the medallists.
They included Tanvi Patri (Badminton), Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada (Judo), Shourya Ambure (Athletics), Gunjan (Boxing) and Tirthank Pegu (Swimming).

Nine of India’s 17 athletes returned with medals, while swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu created history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games.
India’s 10-medal tally was surpassed only by its 13-medal performance at the 2018 Youth Olympics.
Boxing emerged as India’s biggest success story, with Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei winning gold in the boys’ 50kg category and Gunjan claiming the top podium finish in the girls’ 48kg category.
The two victories gave India its first-ever gold medals in boxing at the Youth Olympic Games and marked the country’s first boxing gold double at the competition.
With two gold medals, India also recorded its second-highest gold medal tally in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games.
The campaign also witnessed several historic achievements across other disciplines.
Shourya Ambure became the first Indian athlete to win an athletics medal at the Youth Olympic Games, claiming bronze in the girls’ 100m hurdles.
Taniya secured silver in girls’ freestyle 75kg beach wrestling, giving India its first-ever medal in the discipline at the competition.
India also registered its first medals in swimming and Wushu at the Youth Olympics.
